title: Hotel barbershop, travelling shows and the ukelele
summary: Working beside the hotel and the theatre, he played ukelele and sang in the style of Bing Crosby and the Mills Brothers for pay.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, right down the street, adjacent to the hotel, the barbershop was part of the hotel, I was working in a barber shop -- I don't know whether I mentioned this or not at first. But I was the porter and the shoe shine boy in the barber shop, which had about four seats, four chairs, which catered to all the people in the hotel, and the downtown business people like the dentists, the lawyers, and the what do you call the main building, the city hall?

That's what you find in most all the cities, and all these small towns, they have a little circle there. They call that the downtown area, you know. Well, now the theatre where they had all the shows come in, the travelling shows came in was right next door to the hotel, and they all stayed in there, right. So this gave me this inspiration, and I played the ukelele, you know, four string ukelele, and I'd sing. You know, this was all during the time of Bing Crosby, the Mills Brothers, you know, right?
(Singing). One of those things, Mills Brothers (Humming). You know, right?
So this is all inspiring me and I'm a young boy, you know, I'm having fun, and getting paid for it, getting paid for it, you know, getting paid, spelled g-i-t-t-i-n', gittin' paid.
Gittin' paid, baby. You know, right on.
How long did you do that?
Oh, as I told you, my amnesia was already starting then. I don't know how long it was. It seemed like just a short time. Everything --
As long as your father was --
As long as we were in that town.
